Thanks — did the initial math this morning. Notes:
- February 2027 (non-leap) has 28 days = 40,320 minutes.
- Total full outage = 150 minutes (2h30m). Intermittent degradation we treat per contract as 60 minutes of reduced throughput; contract provides language to convert partial degradation to equivalent downtime at pro-rated rate, which CascadeCrypt has invoked in their request.

Formula we use (per SOW):
credit % = (total_downtime_minutes / minutes_in_month) * 100
credit_amount = min(credit cap, credit % * monthly_committed_amount)

Applying numbers:
- credit % = (210 / 40,320) * 100 = 0.5206% (~0.52%)
- credit_amount = 0.005206 * $12,000 = $62.47

Rounding / policy: we typically round to the nearest dollar for issuance and apply the monthly cap (contract caps credit at 100% of monthly fee which is irrelevant here). The customer asked for a clean figure for accounting; recommend issuing a $62 credit and note the calculation in the memo.

If the team prefers to present a slightly more customer-friendly number we can approve up to $100 without exec sign-off; above that requires finance approval.

I also confirm eligibility — the incident does not fall under force majeure or maintenance exclusion (ops confirmed it was a runtime regression).

- Rishi
General Counsel (acting on contract terms)
